grh_248eab421b308e8daaef.title: Chain Letter
paragraphs: Dr. Christian and Judy argue over why people perpetuate chain letters, with Christian blaming fear and Judy believing money is the stronger motive. To test the question they send one to their financially struggling friend Tom Holland, whose advertising agency is close to failure. Tom himself despises chain letters, but his superstitious wife Bertha secretly sends copies in hopes of bringing him luck. One copy is addressed in Tom's name to Jack Douglas, the Old Silver cigarette representative whose account Tom desperately needs, even though Douglas has just declared that people who send chain letters are fools. Tom, Bertha, Christian and Judy scramble to recover the damaging letter. In the middle of the crisis, however, the repeated idea of a chain gives Tom the advertising hook he has been unable to find: a slogan linking chain smoking with Old Silver cigarettes. Douglas loves the campaign and awards Tom the major account, joking that he knew Tom was intelligent when Tom said he had thrown a chain letter away. The experiment nearly ruins Tom, but the chain letter accidentally supplies the idea that saves his business.

The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Bill Shember as writer and Bob Anderson as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 24 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.514e831176595875|Vaseline Hair Tonic]] and [[org|org.7d8a0c9d85754f41|Vaseline Lip Ice]].

grh_24eff503c22fd7629f99.title: Spring Is Here
paragraphs: Shy Terry Clayton loves Betty but cannot bring himself to compete with glamorous millionaire Stacey Hayden, so Mary Jane tries to manufacture enough romance to make Terry act. When Stacey proposes an elopement, Terry finally attempts to chase them down, only to find Betty has already returned: a kiss from Stacey produced none of the romance she expected. grh_248541ee2d3adabcb514.title: Red Lawson's Revenge
paragraphs: Red Lawson tracks down Britt's friend Dan to avenge a brother Dan killed years earlier during an outlaw ambush. Lawson does not want a fair gunfight; he wants Dan terrified and eventually invades the family farm, using Dan and Mary's baby as leverage.
